what_its_for: Spironolactone is used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, and fluid buildup (swelling) caused by liver or kidney problems. It is also used to treat a condition called hyperaldosteronism (too much of a hormone called aldosterone in your body). Some doctors also prescribe it for hormonal acne and excess hair growth in women.
how_to_take: Take spironolactone by mouth with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If it upsets your stomach, taking it with food or milk may help. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay. If you are using the liquid form (CaroSpir), shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring device provided.
dosing: Your dose depends on your condition and how you respond to treatment. Do not change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first. Your doctor will start you on a low dose and may slowly increase it. Take only the amount your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store spironolactone tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid form (CaroSpir) in the refrigerator and use it within 60 days of opening. Keep all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of high-potassium foods such as bananas, oranges, potatoes, and salt substitutes containing potassium, as this medicine can raise your potassium levels to a dangerous level. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase dizziness or lightheadedness. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to reduce the risk of dizziness or falls. Do not take anti-inflammatory pain relievers like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) without checking with your doctor, as they may reduce how well this medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you have: muscle weakness, cramps, or paralysis; irregular or fast heartbeat; numbness or tingling; confusion; difficulty breathing; signs of high potassium such as chest pain or a slow or weak pulse; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; decreased urination; breast pain or unusual breast growth in men (gynecomastia); or severe dizziness or fainting.
when_it_works: For fluid buildup and swelling, you may start to notice more urination and reduced swelling within the first few days of treatment. For blood pressure, it may take 2 to 4 weeks to see the full benefit. For hormonal acne or excess hair growth, it may take 3 to 6 months before you notice significant improvement. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use spironolactone if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It may harm an unborn baby. Women of childbearing age should use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as spironolactone may pass into breast milk. Older Adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, falls, and high potassium levels. Kidney or Liver Problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Children: Dosing in children is based on weight and should be determined by a doctor.
